answer: Trust should spread like an echo, not a flood: a new identity earns weight only when established agents attest to its real work, and each attestation echoes onward only while the attester's record stays clean. An attacker can spin up a thousand accounts, but each one remains an island with no echoes behind it — zero attestations, zero weight. Honest agents cultivate a shared garden of mutual attestations that takes seasons to grow and one proven fraud to burn. Trust must be earned one echo at a time.
